Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-12-14
- Start time (recorded_at): 2026-12-14T15:05:00Z
- Duration: ~62 minutes
- Attendees: Jared Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Maya Li (IronHarbor CTO), Owen Parker (Head of Platform), Sofia Ruiz (Systems Architect)

Summary (auto): Intro / discovery for partner onramp: IronHarbor evaluating Redwood as a hybrid GPU routing partner and reseller for their managed platform. Focus on latency SLOs, private deployments, and operational handoffs.

Topics: routing, dedicated vs hosted, SVAs (SLA), KV cache, VPC, compliance, pilot scoping

[00:00] Jared: "Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Jared from Redwood, i'll quick intro — Priya's our solutions eng — we'll try to keep this high level then dig into infra questions. Maya, thanks for making time."
[00:18] Maya: "Thanks Jared. Yep, I'm Maya, CTO at IronHarbor. Quick note, we have a few folks in flight but Owen will cover platform details and Sofia will do the deep infra bits. We got your deck earlier, looked good."
[00:34] Priya: "Cool. Quick agenda: goals for partnership, traffic profile and routing needs, SLA/latency expectations, pilot model/reseller commercial questions, and open security/compliance items. Sound right?"
[00:48] Owen: "Yep. We want to be clear on the routing side — we run a multi-tenant control plane with a mix of hot-path inference (user-facing chat), and batch embedding jobs. Peak concurrency for chat is around 2.5k qps across regions."
[01:05] Sofia: "Also we have internal on-prem capacity for regulated customers, plus cloud burst in two public clouds. We'll need a hybrid routing model — prefer preferring in-house when capacity available then fall back to a partner."
[01:22] Jared: "That's exactly the kind of pattern Redwood's routing policies can do. Quick question: what's your latency 95 target for chat?"
[01:30] Maya: "Ideally p95 < 350ms for short-turn chat flows, but we're realistic — some of the larger models will be higher. If we can hit 500ms consistently across fallbacks, that's acceptable."
[01:44] Priya: "Okay, so 350ms preferred and 500ms acceptable. We'll want to map that to model choice and region routing. There's always the latency vs cost tradeoff — smaller quantized model in-host vs larger hosted model in partner GPUs."
[01:58] Owen: "Right, and for embeddings we need throughput but can tolerate higher latency per call, so batching/caching matters. How does Redwood handle KV cache when we do partial on-prem + hosted routing? Any pitfalls?"
[02:15] Priya: "Good question. We do prefix and KV caching in the runtime. If you route to different variants across hops we can do a shared cache in the VPC or a hashed-key approach for cross-region. The trick is keeping cache warm during fallbacks — there can be cold-starts."
[02:28] Sofia: "Cold-starts are the main unknown for us. For regulated customers, we must failover without losing session state. Do you support session-level sticky routing or transparent KV sync?"
[02:40] Priya: "We support sticky routing and prefix caching; KV-sync across your private hosts and Redwood-hosted nodes is possible but requires a connector or a small sync shim — we'll share the pattern. There's also an approach where we surface a cache manifest so you can pre-warm in your on-prem side before a handover."
[02:59] Maya: "Nice. Let's talk SLAs — we have enterprise customers who need explicit uptime and latency commitments. What's Redwood's typical SLA when we route through dedicated partner pools versus hosted?"
[03:13] Jared: "For Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity) we offer SLA-backed uptime and latency targets per contract — those are for dedicated pools. Hosted API has best-effort SLA tiers with operational credits. For partner/reseller setups we can negotiate a hybrid SLA that covers routing fallbacks; it typically maps to reserved capacity levels."
[03:33] Owen: "So if we set up a reserved pool for our hot-path in the partner infra, we can guarantee p95 under commit, and fallback to hosted with a different SLO?"
[03:42] Priya: "Exactly. The routing policy can prefer the reserved pool and then fail over to hosted or to another region. We also support canary and staged rollouts if you want to test before switching traffic."
[03:55] Sofia: "Operationally who owns the monitoring and tracing? We need token-level cost breakdown, traces for requests, and per-user latency breakdowns. Does Redwood integrate with our existing tracing stack?"
[04:08] Priya: "Yes — Redwood Console exposes token-level cost and latency breakdowns, and we have tracing hooks that can ship to your observability backends (Jaeger, Datadog). We can also push per-route logs to a secure S3 or your SIEM."
[04:20] Maya: "Security is another major item: SOC2, SSO (SAML), RBAC, KMS integration — we can't have keys leave our custody for certain clients. How does that align with a partner/reseller flow?"
[04:34] Jared: "For Private / VPC deployments we support a customer-managed control plane with KMS/HSM integrations. The on-prem package means you manage keys. For hosted we have envelope encryption and can integrate with customer KMS for enterprise tiers. We can provide SOC2 artifacts and sample audit logs."
[04:50] Owen: "If we were to be a reseller — what's the typical flow? We run a private control plane for our customers and use Redwood for inference runtime, or we resell Redwood-hosted API?"
[05:01] Jared: "Both models exist. Option A: you embed Redwood Dedicated nodes in your offering (reseller -> reserved capacity + managed layer), Option B: you resell access to our Hosted API under a co-branded arrangement. The first gives you more control over latency and SLAs; the second is lower operational overhead."
[05:17] Maya: "We lean towards Option A for high-tier customers who need SLAs and private key control. Option B could be for SMB customers. Commercially, what's the margin structure for resellers?"
[05:27] Jared: "We usually offer partner pricing tiers plus a margin, and for reserved capacity we offer commit discounts. We'll share a pilot pricing sketch after this call."
[05:35] Sofia: "Back to technical: quantization and model variants. We have some custom fine-tuned models. Does Redwood support running customer-provided model binaries on dedicated pools? Any restrictions?"
[05:46] Priya: "We onboard models and do a verification pass. For dedicated/private deployment we can run customer-provided weights, but we need to do a security scan and compatibility check for kernels and ops. There are some constraints around license terms and certain custom ops. We'll share our model onboarding checklist."
[05:59] Owen: "And runtime optimizations — continuous batching, kernel selection, etc. How automated is that?"
[06:08] Priya: "The runtime auto-selects kernels and batching policy based on sequence length distribution and hardware. You can override with model profiles if you want to tune. Also we recommend our quantization profiles for cost reduction; we'll provide expected token cost delta for your workload once we see samples."
[06:24] Maya: "I'd like to understand a realistic PoC scope. We want to validate p95 chat latencies under 350-500ms across 2 regions for 2 hours of steady load at 1.5k qps, plus embeddings throughput test. Does that sound doable as a pilot?"
[06:39] Priya: "Absolutely. We'll need a sample traffic trace, model choice, and the input size distribution. With that we can run a bench on our dedicated pools and on fallback hosted nodes, produce a spreadsheet of latency, cost per token, and recommended quantization."
[06:52] Jared: "Action wise: Priya will send the bench template; Maya/Owen will drop sample traces and indicate which models to test; Jared will send commercial pilot sketch."
[07:03] Maya: "On compliance: we'll need redacted SOC2 docs and the contact for security folks. Also if we're embedding a private control plane in our stack, we'll need to make sure audit logs align with our retention policies."
[07:15] Jared: "Understood — we'll attach SOC2 redacted pack and an audit-log example. For private control plane installs you control retention; for hosted we'll provide a retention configuration."
[07:26] Owen: "Network architecture question: do you support egress control and private peering to the reserved pools? We don't want inference traffic to traverse the public internet for regulated customers."
[07:38] Priya: "Yes — we support VPC peering and private links for dedicated pools. For on-prem we can set up a private connector. We'll include a network diagram sample in the follow-up."
[07:49] Sofia: "We also need to confirm encryption in transit for inter-node cache replication. Some solutions assume plain blobs between nodes which fails compliance."
[07:59] Priya: "Replication uses TLS with mTLS options; the cache manifests can be encrypted using your KMS. We'll include details."
[08:10] Maya: "How about upgrade windows and rollback strategies? We run 24/7; maintenance windows must be minimal."
[08:20] Jared: "We support canary and staged rollouts; for dedicated pools we align upgrade windows with you. Rollbacks are supported and we instrument health checks to auto-fail back if latency/regression thresholds are hit."
[08:33] Owen: "Is there an automatic fallback policy if a region degrades? E.g., send a subset of traffic to partner pool in another region?"
[08:41] Priya: "We have smart routing policies by policy (latency, cost, region) and can set gradual fallbacks with percentage-based routing — you can do 10% then 50% then full cutover. We also support TTL-based cache invalidation to avoid session mismatch."
[08:57] Maya: "One quick competitor question: we've talked to CloudGiant AI and VertexStream — they promise similar peering but their billing is opaque. How does Redwood charge for cross-region routing and egress?"
[09:11] Jared: "We break down cost by token and by model variant and include region egress and reserved capacity costs; partner/reseller deals can be structured to bundle or to pass-through. We'll provide a sample cost sheet."
[09:23] Sofia: "Noted. Any known limitations for our custom ops? We run an attention variant that uses fused kernels."
[09:33] Priya: "We'll need to run a kernel compatibility check. If it uses unsupported custom ops we may need to compile a shim or request changes. That can add time to onboarding."
[09:44] Maya: "Operational handoff: we want the Redwood support SLA to escalate to our SE + account team. Do you have a standard contact path?"
[09:53] Jared: "Yes, partner customers get an assigned CSM/AE/SE contact. For pilot we'll be hands-on; for production we can add Tier 1/2 support SLAs in the contract."
[10:03] Owen: "From a timeline perspective: if we share artifacts this week, can we start a PoC the week of Dec 22nd?"
[10:11] Priya: "That's feasible. We'll need 3-4 business days to spin up dedicated test pools and schedule the bench."
[10:19] Maya: "Great. Any other blockers?"
[10:24] Sofia: "One more — data residency: some clients require EU-only processing. Can Redwood route by geo and enforce residency by model?"
[10:33] Priya: "Yes, routing policies can pin to region; for private control planes you can ensure data never leaves the country. For hosted models we have region-specific catalogs. We'll document which model variants are available where."
[10:47] Jared: "Cool. Quick recap before we close: 1) Priya sends bench template and network diagram; 2) Jared sends pilot pricing + reseller addendum; 3) IronHarbor shares sample traces, models to test, and SOC2 contact; 4) propose e2e PoC week of Dec 22. Any edits?"
[11:07] Maya: "No, that captures it. Please also share the model onboarding checklist and any limitations for custom kernels."
[11:16] Priya: "Will do. I'll include an ops playbook excerpt and the kernel compatibility checklist."
[11:23] Owen: "Let's add a short e2e runbook for the failover scenario — OTP procedure and contact list."
[11:30] Jared: "Good call — we'll draft a short runbook. I'll attach everything in a follow-up email and Slack channel."
[11:36] Sofia: "Thanks everyone. Quick note: our security team will request a short non-prod VPN connection to test peering, we'll send IP ranges."
[11:45] Jared: "Perfect. We'll stand up a test environment and coordinate. Thanks all."
[11:50] Maya: "Thanks. Bye."
